name: Des Moines
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Des Moines: insurance and agency fraud, annuity carrier diligence, staff misconduct, agribusiness risk.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Des Moines, scoped from Nashville: factual research for insurers, annuity carriers, banks and their counsel in one of the most insurance-concentrated metros in the United States, from claims and agency fraud to diligence on acquisitions, managers and agribusiness counterparties.
intro: Des Moines is the capital and largest city of Iowa, with a population of 212,086 in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate and a six-county metropolitan area that counted 709,466 people in the 2020 census. Insurance and financial services drive its economy. According to the Greater Des Moines Partnership, 82 insurance companies are headquartered in the region, which has the highest concentration of insurance employment among US metros, and finance and insurance contributed 25.3 billion dollars of the region's 90 billion dollar GDP in 2024. Wells Fargo employs more than 11,000 people locally and Principal about 5,600. Nationwide, Wellmark Blue Cross Blue Shield of Iowa, Athene, F&G Annuities and Life and John Deere Financial also have major operations.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Des Moines largely because of that concentration of insurers, annuity writers and financial services operations. Carriers and their counsel need facts on suspicious claims, agency and producer misconduct, and employees or vendors suspected of diverting funds. Acquirers, reinsurers and distribution partners of life and annuity companies headquartered in the region examine their owners, managers and related parties. Large back-office and technology operations, including data centres built by major technology companies, raise questions about insider misconduct and data handling. The surrounding agricultural economy brings agribusiness lenders, insurers and buyers who need background on farm operators, grain and equipment counterparties.

matters.title: Insurance claims and agency fraud
matters.text: Factual research for carriers and their counsel on suspicious life, health, property and crop claims, and on agents or producers suspected of misrepresentation, premium diversion or churning, including links between claimants, providers, agencies and the businesses that profit from questionable payments.

matters.title: Life and annuity carrier diligence
matters.text: Background research on the owners, directors, managers and related parties behind life and annuity companies and their affiliates headquartered in the region, for acquirers, reinsurers, lenders and distribution partners assessing governance, conflicts of interest, litigation history and reputational exposure.

matters.title: Internal misconduct in financial operations
matters.text: Supporting counsel and compliance teams in large banking, insurance and processing operations with fact-finding on suspected expense fraud, vendor kickbacks, conflicts of interest or misuse of customer data, using documents, interviews arranged by counsel and public-record research on the individuals and companies involved.

matters.title: Agribusiness counterparty research
matters.text: Background research on farm operators, grain dealers, equipment dealers and agricultural lenders connected to central Iowa, covering ownership, liens and judgments of record, litigation and adverse media, so lenders, insurers and buyers understand who they are dealing with before extending credit or cover.

matters.title: Executive and board candidate vetting
matters.text: Lawful background research on senior hires and board candidates for insurers, financial firms and other Des Moines employers, covering career claims, directorships, regulatory actions, litigation and public statements, carried out in line with the Fair Credit Reporting Act where it applies to the engagement.

local_context.title: Iowa investigator licensing rules
local_context.text: Iowa regulates private investigation, private security and bail enforcement under Iowa Code chapter 80A and administrative rules 661, chapter 121. Agencies providing contracted services in Iowa need a state licence from the Department of Public Safety, whose Program Services Bureau handles licensing from Des Moines, and individuals performing regulated work need a state-issued identification card obtained through a licensed agency. Any field work in Iowa is therefore coordinated with an Iowa-licensed agency.

local_context.title: State capital institutions
local_context.text: As Iowa's capital, Des Moines is the seat of state government and its departments, including the Department of Public Safety. The Iowa Insurance Division, the state's insurance regulator, is the source cited for the region's count of insurance headquarters, and its records of company licensing and regulatory actions are relevant to diligence on carriers and agencies. State-level records and regulatory filings are a starting point for many matters.

local_context.title: Courts and dispute forums
local_context.text: Litigation involving Des Moines companies and residents is heard in Iowa state courts and, where federal jurisdiction applies, in federal court. We have not verified the structure and locations of these courts for this page, so engagements confirm with the client's counsel which court records to search, and in what form they are available, before research begins. No arbitration centre based in Des Moines has been identified.

local_context.title: Insurance innovation ecosystem
local_context.text: The Greater Des Moines Partnership points to the Global Insurance Accelerator, which marked its twelfth year in 2026, and the Global Insurance Symposium, which has drawn more than 5,000 attendees from over 20 countries. These bring early-stage insurtech companies and international partners into contact with Des Moines carriers, which often calls for background research on founders, investors and technology vendors before partnerships.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Des Moines, TDSC begins by framing the question in insurance or financial services terms: whether a claim or agency is genuine, who controls a carrier or affiliate, or what an employee did with funds or data. Research is conducted from Nashville, drawing on state and federal court records, Iowa business and regulatory records, insurance regulatory actions and open sources. Where interviews, surveillance or other field steps are justified, TDSC coordinates with an agency licensed in Iowa under chapter 80A and works through the client's counsel. Consumer report rules under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and insurers' data obligations are reviewed at the outset, and personal information is collected only as the matter requires.

faqs.q: Can TDSC help an insurer investigate a suspicious claim in central Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. We research the claimant, related businesses and providers, prior claims and litigation of record, and public information that bears on the facts of the loss. Where interviews, scene work or surveillance are justified, we coordinate with an Iowa-licensed agency and the carrier's counsel, and we keep the work consistent with the insurer's claims-handling obligations.

faqs.q: Who licenses private investigators in Iowa?
faqs.a: The Iowa Department of Public Safety licenses private investigation, private security and bail enforcement agencies under Iowa Code chapter 80A, and individuals doing regulated work carry a state identification card issued through a licensed agency. TDSC does not hold an Iowa licence, so any regulated work in Iowa is carried out by an appropriately licensed Iowa agency.

faqs.q: What does diligence on a Des Moines life or annuity company involve?
faqs.a: We identify the ultimate owners, directors and key managers of the company and its affiliates, then review regulatory actions, litigation, related-party arrangements and reputation from public sources. The aim is to give acquirers, reinsurers and distribution partners a clear view of governance and conflicts, alongside the financial and actuarial review done by other advisers.

faqs.q: Can you vet agribusiness borrowers or counterparties in Iowa?
faqs.a: Yes. We research ownership, business registrations, liens and judgments of record, litigation, bankruptcies and adverse media on farm operators, dealers and agribusiness firms. Where collateral such as equipment or stored grain matters, we advise counsel on what public records can show and when physical verification by a licensed local professional is warranted.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Des Moines?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Des Moines. Most research is conducted remotely using public and lawfully available records. Where field work in Iowa is needed, we coordinate with appropriately licensed Iowa professionals and the client's counsel rather than acting directly.
